questions.text: FIXTURE: Which statement best describes a strict liability offence?
options: A. The prosecution must prove intention.
B. Mens rea need not be proved, but honest and reasonable mistake of fact is a defence.
C. No defence is ever available.

option_rationales.A: Tempting because most offences need mens rea, but not strict liability.
option_rationales.B: Correct: He Kaw Teh v The Queen.
option_rationales.D: Recklessness is a form of mens rea.

questions.explanation: Strict liability removes the need to prove mens rea but keeps honest and reasonable mistake.

questions.text: FIXTURE: Explain how bail laws balance the rights of the accused with community safety.

criteria.descriptor: Explains the balance with reference to the bail test
Explains with some reference to the law

required_elements: Presumption of innocence and liberty of the accused
The unacceptable risk test under the Bail Act 2013 (NSW)
questions.model: Bail laws decide whether an accused person is released before trial. The Bail Act 2013 (NSW) requires a bail authority to assess whether there is an unacceptable risk, which protects the presumption of innocence while allowing remand when the community would be at risk. On balance the law is largely effective.
questions.currency_note: Before you rely on this: the Bail Act 2013 (NSW) has been amended several times; check the current tests.

stimulus.title: FIXTURE hypothetical scenario: Sam's trial

required_elements: The prosecution bears the burden of proof
questions.model: The prosecution must prove each element beyond reasonable doubt; Sam does not have to prove innocence.
